note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent judge) after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap}. RFC 8210 Section 9.1 reads 'User authentication MUST be supported; host authentication MAY be supported.  Implementations MAY support password authentication.' The sentence binds both ends of an SSH transport, and the router end is Ze's role. Section 9 makes SSHv2 a transport Ze may offer, and no owner decision declines it, so the absent SSH transport is an implementation gap, not an exclusion: the earlier not-applicable verdict, which read 'no SSH transport code exists' as no code path, recorded an unimplemented feature as an exclusion. internal/component/bgp/plugins/rpki/rtr_session.go::RTRSession.connectAndSync dials TCP and, for a cache configured with it, hands the connection to internal/component/bgp/plugins/rpki/rtr_tls.go::RTRSession.startTLS; no code offers an SSH transport, so neither host nor password authentication exists.
